newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends lower, Brent lethargic.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends lower, Brent lethargic.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed the week $1.50 a tonne lower at $213.75 a tonne, reversing a rally earlier this week on perceptions of tight supplies on both sides of the Atlantic.
Brokers said the oil complex was feeling the brunt of weak gasoline futures in New York.
"It has gone out with a bit of a whimper. The market has a very muted feel to it today.
"The only thing which is ringing any alarm bells is gasoline which continues to be unsupported and unwanted. It's beginning to put a bit of pressure on heat," a futures broker said.

NYMEX gasoline, which tumbled almost two cents per gallon on Thursday, was down 1.02 cents at 60.30 cents at 1702 GMT. London dealers said movement of gasoline from Europe into the U.S. market was depressing the contract.
The broker said that if gasoline continued to be under pressure and heating oil went below a $66-$66.30 trendline, there was the chance of a further downside.
NYMEX crude activity was dominated by the expiry on Friday of the October WTI contract.
IPE November Brent was down 13 cents at $21.78 a barrel at 1712 GMT, having traded in a tight range throughout the day.
It managed an intra-day high of $21.97 earlier in the session.
"I think crude was in a consolidative phase today, while the expiring WTI is ominously quiet. I wonder if it is a precursor to a potential pullback," the broker said.
